History of Present Illness:
55-year-old woman. Three days of left lower abdominal pain and loose stools. No recent travel or antibiotic exposure.

Physical Examination:
Focal left lower-quadrant tenderness; abdomen soft elsewhere. Temperature 37.7 C; heart rate 94/min; BP 122/74 mmHg; respiratory rate 20/min; SpO2 98% on room air.

Laboratory Tests:
WBC: 12.9 10^9/L (reference 4.0-11.0)
Hemoglobin: 13.5 g/dL (reference 12.0-17.5)
Platelets: 227 10^9/L (reference 150-400)
Sodium: 137 mmol/L (reference 135-145)
Potassium: 3.9 mmol/L (reference 3.5-5.0)
Creatinine: 0.9 mg/dL (reference 0.6-1.3)
CRP: 54 mg/L (reference <5)
Lipase: 33 U/L (reference 13-60)
ALT: 29 U/L (reference 7-45)
AST: 26 U/L (reference 10-40)
Alkaline phosphatase: 87 U/L (reference 40-130)
Total bilirubin: 0.7 mg/dL (reference 0.2-1.2)

Imaging Findings:
CT abdomen/pelvis: focal sigmoid wall thickening around diverticula with marked adjacent fat stranding. No diffuse colitis or collection.
